mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor force participation rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a bearish S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in one month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: In a 200-day window, the correlation between PAYEMS change and 20-day SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand away from manufacturing toward housing, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in a month while INDPRO decreases by >2%
regime_hint: transition from industrial to housing demand dominance
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 5-day ahead return of SPX is not positively related to the HOUST-INDPRO interaction (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp and persistent decline in the ISM non-manufacturing index (not directly observable in the provided series; therefore this sketch is invalid per the observable constraints) — thus, instead: A multi-month drop in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests supply-side contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns when sustained for two months.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >4% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain non-negative during the identified INDPRO contraction period (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month while the 10-year Treasury yield (not directly observable) is assumed stable, it signals inflationary pressure that tends to drive investors into safe assets, producing a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: In 12 months of similar CPIAUCSL surprises, the 60-day SPX returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with a regime of weak labor demand, which historically precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the period UNRATE > 5%, the 20-day SPX forward return is positive in over 70% of instances (failure of the hypothesis).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in retail sales proxies (not directly observable; thus using GDPC1 as a broad demand indicator) and a decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) suggests shifting demand toward consumer goods, which predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >3% in a month while INDPRO decreases by >2%
failure_condition: Over 24 months, the 5-day SPX returns are not positively correlated with the GDPC1-INDPRO interaction (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional effect where S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positively related to the interaction between the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS and the 12-month change in UNRATE only during periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS up, UNRATE down). This interaction is inactive in loosening regimes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS 12m change > 0 and UNRATE 12m change < 0 (tightening regime)
failure_condition: In tightening regimes as defined, the 20-day SPX forward return is not significantly higher than in loosening regimes (p > 0.05 in t-test).
